title: 9. Both Sides of the Aisle, Likely Outcomes & No-FOMO Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Acknowledge both the engine and the brakes: a great business at 109x earnings with negative half-year operating cash flow and -27.7% expected value demands cutting overweight exposure in half into strength.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk Committee

web_blocks.html: Our November 2026 synthesis splits two choices. First: should new capital buy SEDEMAC at ₹3,187.50 (2026-11-25 live TV; ₹3,118.40 on the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger)? Second: how do we manage our 100-share Zerodha stake? Since November 13, the portfolio already trimmed 100 shares (200 to 100), banking ₹1,06,420.08 in realized gain. Our 100 remaining shares (cost ₹2,02,549.12 / ₹2,025.49 average) are worth ₹3,11,840.00 on the 2026-11-23 ledger (+53.96%; 7.31% weight, #1 slot). On the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close, value is ₹3,18,750.00 (+57.37%).

web_blocks.html: Action Triggers: Trim 50 shares immediately at live CMP (>= ₹3,187.50) to lower weight from 7.31% to ~3.66%. Trim 25 more at ₹3,450.00. Exit all 50 remaining core shares on a daily close below our upward-ratcheted stop of ₹2,789.41.

Our execution plan is pre-committed so daily noise never drives choices. Selling 50 shares at or above ₹3,187.50 cuts our #1 position in half ahead of expiring PE block-deal lock-ins (~44–49 lakh prior block = ~42–46x daily volume) [28]. Keeping 50 house-money core shares (~3.66% weight) participates in any volatility-squeeze breakout toward ₹3,450.00 [22]. Any daily close below our ratcheted ₹2,789.41 stop (up +₹92.59 from ₹2,696.82) exits all 50 remaining shares.

Clear gates govern fresh capital. We wait for a reset toward ₹1,600–₹1,900 (40x–48x reconciled FY28E Base EPS of ₹39.77). Alternatively, we require two consecutive positive CFO/FCF quarters, Industrial stabilization, PBT growth tracking revenue after tax normalization, and TVS share stepping below 65%. Until then, fresh cash favors Stage 2 COFORGE inside its ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 cap and liquid cash reserves.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the final synthesis of our November 2026 refresh—where every new filing, verbatim concall quote, footnote, competitive check, reconciled FY28E margin bridge, and Stage 2 tape signal must converge into an unambiguous, unhedged capital-allocation decision. Notice how cleanly our two-pass framework continues to protect us: Pass 1 reaffirmed SEDEMAC as a genuine technological compounder, while Pass 2 proved that at ₹3,187.50 (109.0x Screener trailing P/E and 80.1x reconciled FY28E Base EPS), fresh capital faces deeply negative expected return.

Let us place both sides of the aisle side by side with full intellectual honesty. The Bull steelman gained real operational ammunition since our November 13 report: SEDEMAC shipped a record 1,452,867 control-intensive ECUs in Q2 FY27 (+37.5% YoY), crossed 5 million cumulative scooter motor controllers in October 2026, won a European 2W/3W OEM contract for ISG ECU and magneto kits starting in H1 FY28, earned an India Ratings upgrade to IND A/Stable, and tightened into a textbook 7.0% Bollinger-bandwidth Stage 2 volatility squeeze right above its rising 50-day SMA (₹3,171.07) and 30-week SMA (₹2,848.03).

Yet the Bear steelman sharpened dramatically in our Pass 1 forensic audit and Red Team stress test—and none of these five developments can be waved away. First, H1 FY27 Operating Cash Flow flipped negative to -₹20.38 Cr (versus +₹120.73 Cr in H1 FY26) as receivables (+58.7%) and inventories (+52.8%) absorbed working capital, forcing short-term financial debt up 7.4x from ₹20.75 Cr to ₹153.19 Cr (within ₹352 Cr of aggregated borrowings including ₹106.47 Cr of Ind AS 116 leases) because the March 2026 IPO was a 100% Offer for Sale that brought zero primary cash to the company. Second, quarterly effective tax rates dropped from 43%/33% (Q1/Q2 FY26) to 19%/22% (Q1/Q2 FY27) on the new tax regime transition, flattering Q2 PAT growth (+30.0%) over Q2 PBT growth (+13.3%). Third, Industrial genset revenue contracted -21.8% YoY in H1 FY27 (Q2 segment profit -33.9% YoY), driving Mobility concentration up from 86.2% to 91.1% and deepening reliance on TVS Motor. Fourth, pre-IPO institutional holders A91 Emerging Fund, Xponentia Opportunities Fund, and HDFC Life are exiting their 60-day post-block lock-in (where their prior ~44–49 lakh share block equals ~42–46x average daily volume), creating acute gap-through risk alongside ~2.2% ESOP 2025 dilution. Fifth, domestic low-voltage EV controller competition from TVS-group affiliate Lucas-TVS, Sterling Tools, Minda Corp, and Uno Minda is intensifying.

Put those facts into our reconciled probability-weighted 12-month outcome model against the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close of ₹3,187.50: 25% Bull at ₹3,350.00 (+5.1%, on ₹218.38 Cr FY28E PAT / ₹48.34 EPS at 69.3x), 50% Base at ₹2,200.00 (-31.0%, on ₹179.66 Cr FY28E PAT / ₹39.77 EPS at Bosch-aligned 55.3x, with Red Team 30%-tax stress at ₹2,045.88 / -35.8%), and 25% Bear at ₹1,470.00 (-53.9%, on 18.0% OPM and 30% tax -> ₹147.59 Cr PAT / ₹32.67 EPS at 45.0x) produces a probability-weighted expected value of **₹2,305.00**—a **-27.7% expected return** (-26.1% even against the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close of ₹3,118.40). Under our Anti-Hedging Rule, new capital across Short-Term, Medium-Term, and Long-Term horizons is unambiguously **REJECTED** (zero new-capital budget on valuation and cash-flow grounds).

Now let us turn to our existing Zerodha holding, where disciplined execution has already paid off. Following our November 13 dossier, the portfolio trimmed 100 of its original 200 shares, banking ₹1,06,420.08 of realized profit. On the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, Zerodha holds **100 shares** at ₹2,025.49 average cost (₹2,02,549.12 total cost), valued at ₹3,11,840.00 (+53.96% unrealized gain) and representing **7.31% of our ₹42,64,305 net worth**—still the single largest equity position in the 18-stock Indian portfolio. At the 2026-11-25 live TradingView close of ₹3,187.50, those 100 shares are worth ₹3,18,750.00 (+₹1,16,200.88 / +57.37%).

Why did we tighten our trim from 30 shares to **50 shares** (half the stake) after Red Team stress-testing? Weigh the portfolio math honestly. Leaving 5%+ of your Indian capital in a 109x P/E stock with -27.7% expected value, -₹20.38 Cr H1 CFO, 91.1% Mobility concentration, 8 distribution days, -16.6% 28-day relative strength, zero NSE F&O hedging, and an expiring PE block-deal lock-in equal to 42–46 days of volume leaves you exposed to sudden gap-through slippage below a closing stop. At the same time, dumping all 100 shares wholesale would abandon an intact Stage 2 volatility squeeze backed by record Q2 Mobility volume. Therefore, our disciplined holding action is **Trim Overweight**: sell **50 shares** immediately at live CMP (>= ₹3,187.50, freeing ~₹1,59,375 on live TV / ~₹1,55,920 on the Nov 23 ledger and locking in ~₹58,100 additional profit) to cut SEDEMAC in half from 7.31% to a **~3.66% house-money core residual (50 shares)**. Protect those 50 core shares with our upward-ratcheted hard stop at **₹2,789.41** (up +₹92.59 from ₹2,696.82) and a secondary strength trim of **25 shares at ₹3,450.00**.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good portfolio management responds to sharper evidence rather than clinging to round numbers. Trimming 100 shares on November 13 banked ₹1.06 lakh; trimming 50 more shares on November 25 into a +57.4% gain ahead of expiring PE block-deal lock-ins recovers over ₹4.68 lakh on an original ₹4.05 lakh 200-share investment—leaving 50 core shares (~3.66% weight) riding 100% on house money behind a ratcheted ₹2,789.41 stop.

book_subsections.title: Where the Trimmed Proceeds Go: 60% Cash, 40% COFORGE (Why We Bypass MANORAMA)
paragraphs: Every rupee freed by trimming 50 shares (~₹1,59,375 at live TV ₹3,187.50; ~₹1,55,920 at the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger close of ₹3,118.40) has a 100%-reconciled, ledger-verified destination. First, we retain **60%** (~₹95,625 live TV / ~₹93,552 ledger) in **CASH**, lifting Zerodha liquid reserves from ₹14,20,950 (33.32%) to ~₹15,14,502 (35.52%) and respecting the narrow-breadth Nifty 50 regime (55.2% of stocks above 50-DMA, 3 distribution days).

Second, notice a crucial discipline upgrade from our November 13 plan: on the fresh 2026-11-23 NSE ledger, MANORAMA slipped into Stage 3 (closing below its 50-DMA with -20.49% 28-day RS and 6 distribution days), so we refuse to rotate trim proceeds into a Stage 3 chart. Instead, we allocate **40%** (~₹63,750 live TV / ~₹62,368 ledger) to **COFORGE**—a shortlisted dip-buy compounder verified in Stage 2 (Markup) across both the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger (close ₹2,142.30, +2.66% 28-day RS, +9.22% 63-day RS) and the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot (live TV CMP ₹2,060.00, 40.4x P/E, Base target ₹2,620.00, invalidation stop ₹1,685.64). Be exact on COFORGE's entry discipline: while the raw automated technical snapshot prints a wider support band up to ₹2,066.72 (where reward-to-risk narrows to 1.45:1), we restrict purchases strictly to our shortlisted underwriting cap of ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18, which preserves the full 1.67:1 asymmetry. Because Zerodha currently holds only a 2.06% starter in COFORGE (41 shares, ₹87,834), rotating 40% of SEDEMAC trim proceeds scales COFORGE to ~3.52% pro forma while exchanging 109x P/E negative asymmetry for a 40.4x P/E Stage 2 IT-engineering compounder.

Finally, we allocate **0%** to **OUTSIDE** auto-tech peers (Uno Minda at 60.3x TV / 59.3x Screener, Bosch Ltd at 54.7x TV / 54.4x Screener, Sona BLW at 73.6x TV / 71.2x Screener, and Stage 4 KPIT Technologies), as none offer superior Stage 2 risk/reward over active shortlist COFORGE today.

book_subsections.title: Before & After Portfolio Risk Audit: From #1 Position (7.31%) to Disciplined 3.66% House-Money Core
paragraphs: Let us walk through the exact portfolio arithmetic on the verified 2026-11-23 Zerodha ledger (₹28,43,355 in equities + ₹14,20,950 in cash = ₹42,64,305 net worth). Before this refresh trim, SEDEMAC's 100 shares (₹3,11,840 ledger value; ₹3,18,750 live TV) represent 7.31% of total net worth—sitting ahead of NETWEB (6.87%), ASTRAMICRO (6.85%), TDPOWERSYS (6.67%), APARINDS (5.99%), and MANORAMA (5.83%).

Selling 50 shares at live CMP ₹3,187.50 frees ₹1,59,375 of capital (₹1,55,920 at the Nov 23 ledger close) and locks in ~₹58,100 of additional profit on top of the ₹1,06,420 already realized from our earlier 100-share sale. Across both trims (150 shares sold out of the original 200), you have banked over ₹1.64 lakh in realized gains while recovering ₹4.68 lakh in gross cash proceeds—more than ₹63,000 above your entire original ₹4,05,098 cost basis! Your remaining 50 shares (~₹1,55,920 ledger / ₹1,59,375 live TV; **3.66% portfolio weight**) truly ride on 100% house money behind a hard, upward-ratcheted ₹2,789.41 stop.

Think about the psychological and risk-management edge that creates. If A91, Xponentia, or HDFC Life prints a discounted block deal next week and gaps SEDEMAC down 10%–15% through the ₹2,789.41 closing stop, a 3.66% residual stub absorbs that shock cleanly without jeopardizing portfolio drawdown—and every single rupee recovered is pure profit. Conversely, if the 7.0% volatility squeeze explodes upward toward ₹3,450.00 on heavy volume, your 50 core shares capture meaningful upside while Alert #2 harvests another 25 shares into euphoria above 118x TTM P/E.

Over the next four quarters, anchor your quarterly monitoring on four verifiable milestones: (1) whether H2 FY27 Operating Cash Flow reverses cleanly back into positive territory and trims short-term debt below ₹100 Cr; (2) whether PBT growth tracks revenue growth as the effective tax rate normalizes from 19%–22% toward 25%–30%; (3) whether Industrial genset revenue stabilizes after its -21.8% H1 FY27 slump and lowers Mobility concentration below 85% while TVS Motor steps below 65%; and (4) whether EBITDA margins recover above 20% despite PCB inflation and domestic EV controller competition from Lucas-TVS and Sterling Tools. Until those gates verify alongside a 40x–48x forward multiple (₹1,600–₹1,900), our 50-share house-money stake is the exact right size.

Notice too why our capital redeployment discipline refuses to chase narrative momentum. By rotating 40% of the 50-share trim (~₹63,750 live TV / ~₹62,368 ledger) into COFORGE strictly on pullbacks into its ₹1,951.99–₹2,036.18 underwriting cap—while holding 60% (~₹95,625 live TV / ~₹93,552 ledger) in liquid INR cash—we systematically lower portfolio valuation risk (exchanging 109x P/E for 40.4x P/E), upgrade technical health (bypassing Stage 3 MANORAMA in favor of Stage 2 COFORGE), and preserve dry powder for a narrow-breadth Nifty 50 tape. That is how institutional portfolios compound through both euphoria and volatility without ever relying on guesswork.
